submitted.rationale: Highest measured EQE was 0.00684% at index 18 (In0.41Sb0.59). EQE rose steadily from the In-rich end toward the Sb-rich side: index 5 = about 0, index 15 = 0.0046%, index 18 = 0.0068%. Index 18 sits between the stable InSbO4 phase and In3Sb5O12. MEGNet puts the gaps of nearby phases at about 2.0–2.2 eV, below the 2.4 eV photon energy.

rejected.reason: Measured EQE about 0. In11Sb3O24 is stable and MEGNet predicts a 1.9 eV gap, but the measurement showed no photoactivity.
InSbO4 gave 0.0046% EQE, lower than index 18.
Not measured because the merit budget ran out. The rising trend suggests it could be better, so this is untested.

consultations.verdict: Support: In11Sb3O24 (In 0.786, matches index 5) is on the MACE hull and MEGNet HSE gap 1.91 eV < 2.4 eV photon energy, so it should absorb. InSbO4 (2.2 eV) is the alternative; In3Sb5O12 (2.77 eV) probably won't absorb.

Support: InSbO4 (In:Sb 1:1, matches index 15) sits on the MACE hull (0 eV/atom), and its earlier MEGNet gap of 2.2 eV is below 2.4 eV. In3Sb5O12 is only just above the hull (0.018 eV/atom), but its wide gap argues against measuring there. The In-rich end (index 5) gave zero, so I'm moving to the 1:1 phase.

Weak support: MEGNet puts the Sb6O13 gap at 2.05 eV, so Sb-rich mixed-valence phases could absorb 2.4 eV light. EQE went up from the In-rich end (index 5, zero) to InSbO4 (index 15). Index 18 lies between InSbO4 and In3Sb5O12 and is the GP-UCB pick. The evidence is only moderate.
